sections.skill: Disclose and manage sponsorships and affiliate links as a creator

questions.prompt: Where should a sponsorship be disclosed in a video?

choices.text: Nowhere, if the creator likes the product
Only in the last second after the video ends
Only in a separate website nobody visits
Clearly, where viewers notice, such as at the start

questions.correct_answer: Clearly, where viewers notice, such as at the start
questions.intro: Creators may earn through SPONSORSHIPS (a brand pays for a mention or video) and AFFILIATE LINKS (a commission on sales). Both are material connections that should be disclosed clearly where viewers will notice, such as saying "This video is sponsored by..." at the start and labeling links. A platform's built-in disclosure tool is not automatically enough. Choose sponsors that fit your audience, agree in writing on deliverables, payment and deadlines, and never make claims about a product you cannot support.

sections.skill: A friend recommending a restaurant she owns

questions.prompt: Why might you feel misled?

choices.text: You did not know about her stake

questions.correct_answer: You did not know about her stake
questions.intro: If a friend raves about a restaurant and later you learn she owns part of it, you might feel misled, even if the food is good. If she says up front, "I own part of this place, but I think you'll love it," you can decide for yourself. Sponsorship disclosure is that up-front sentence, said before the recommendation.
